CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Cancer Center
Department of Hematopathology and Molecular Diagnostics

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient: [redacted name]
Age/Sex: 73-year-old male
MRN: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Bone marrow aspirate
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Myeloma patient requiring cytogenetic analysis

TEST PERFORMED
Interphase Fluorescence In Situ Hybridization (FISH) Panel for Multiple Myeloma

METHODOLOGY
Interphase FISH analysis was performed on CD138+ immunomagnetically purified plasma cells from bone marrow aspirate. Analysis was limited to 50 cells due to sample cellularity. The following probe sets were utilized:

• IGH Dual Color Break Apart Rearrangement Probe (14q32)
• TP53/CEP17 Dual Color Probe (17p13.1/17p11.1-q11.1)
• CDKN2C/CEN1 Dual Color Probe (1p32.3)
• DLEU/LAMP1 Dual Color Probe (13q14/13q34)
• CKS1B/CDKN2C Dual Color Probe (1q21/1p32.3)
• ATM/CEP11 Dual Color Probe (11q22.3/11p11.1-q11.1)
• CEP5/CEP9/CEP15 Tri-Color Probe

RESULTS

Probe				Result				Pattern			Cells Analyzed
IGH (14q32)			Negative			2F (normal)		50
TP53 (17p13.1)			Negative			2R2G (normal)		50
CDKN2C (1p32.3)		Negative			2R2G (normal)		50
DLEU (13q14)			Negative			2R2G (normal)		50
CKS1B (1q21)			Negative			2R2G (normal)		50
ATM (11q22.3)			Negative			2R2G (normal)		50
Chromosome 5			Diploid				2 signals		50
Chromosome 9			Diploid				2 signals		50
Chromosome 15			Diploid				2 signals		50

INTERPRETATION
No IGH rearrangement detected.
No deletion of TP53, CDKN2C or DLEU detected.
Normal diploid pattern for CKS1B, ATM and chromosomes 5, 9, and 15.

No myeloma-associated cytogenetic abnormalities detected in analyzed sample.

TECHNICAL LIMITATIONS
Dual-color break-apart probes cannot detect cryptic insertions or inversions that do not separate the probe signals beyond the resolution of FISH (approximately 200kb). This analysis was performed on CD138+ selected cells; however, the purity of the plasma cell population cannot be guaranteed. The sensitivity of this assay is limited by the number of cells analyzed.

This test was developed and its performance characteristics determined by [redacted location] Cancer Center. It has not been cleared or approved by the FDA. The FDA has determined that such clearance or approval is not necessary.

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD
